newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA PLANS TAX PREFERENCES FOR WASTE RECYCLING.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA PLANS TAX PREFERENCES FOR WASTE RECYCLING.

text.p: Bulgaria pledged tax incentives to companies that recycle domestic, industrial and toxic waste under a draft bill approved by the cabinet on Thursday, the Environment Minister said.
"The government approved a draft law on minimising enviroment pollution, under which tax preferences will be granted to waste recycling companies," Evdokia Maneva told repoters.
Under the draft corporate tax for locally-operating companies licensed to recycle waste would be reduced by the amount of investments they had made in the waste processing installations, Maneva said.
Value added tax (VAT) will be waived for waste recycling services to stimulate companies to process waste. Bulgaria has a 22 percent flat VAT rate.

Each year Bulgarian plants delivered 34.5 million tonnes of industrial waste, including one million tonnes of toxic waste and domestic waste of glass, paper, metals and other recyclable materials amounted to five million tonnes, said Maneva.
Bulgaria now had over 2,000 waste depots, of which only around 720 could be considered in line with the Envirorment Ministry requirements and it had no toxic waste depot, Maneva added.
